finding: The control arm's --ship-gates eval crashed inside publish_agentv_evaluation with Node ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on node_modules/typebox/build/typebox.mjs. Root cause: this checkout's node_modules had @agentv/core/package.json present (a stale/partial install baked into the sandbox image) but a transitive dependency (typebox) was missing its build output. _agentv_runtime's self-heal reuse check in src/slm_training/evals/agentv.py only checked @agentv/core/package.json existence before trusting an install, so it never re-ran npm ci to repair the drift. Manually running `npm ci` at the repo root fixed the immediate environment for this session, but the harness bug (false-positive 'already installed' check) would recur in any other checkout with a similarly stale node_modules. Fixed in commit 9a53ea83c4265629f50bcb490f3abfb142059a8c (evals.agentv v9 -> v10): cross-check node_modules/.package-lock.json against package-lock.json for every non-optional package before reusing an existing install (optional platform-mismatched deps, e.g. darwin/win32 binaries on this linux-x64 sandbox, are excluded since npm legitimately skips those). Added two regression tests (drifted-install-triggers-bootstrap, optional-deps-tolerated) plus updated the four pre-existing runtime tests whose fixtures previously only set up @agentv/core/package.json without a matching lockfile marker; all 14 tests in tests/test_evals/test_agentv.py pass.
